newsitem.title: RUSSIA: No reason to worry about Yeltsin health - spokesman.
newsitem.headline: No reason to worry about Yeltsin health - spokesman.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin, recovering from pneumonia, is dealing with affairs of state and there is no need to worry about his health, senior officials said on Monday.

"There is no reason for alarm over the president's health," Ekho Moskvy radio quoted press spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky as saying. He said Yeltsin was working on his planned address to both houses of the Russian parliament, due to be delivered at the end of next month.
Interfax news agency quoted Prime Minister Viktor Chernnomyrdin as saying Yeltsin was looking at both domestic and international policy.
"He is dealing with the basic questions of state policy, both domestic and foreign," Chernomyrdin said. "The president is returning to good form and will be in good form."
Yeltsin, 65, has been convalescing from double pneumonia at a government rest home outside Moscow and Chernomyrdin said last week that he would be back in the Kremlin soon.
But doctors, urging the president not to rush his return to work, say he should wait two or three weeks.

Russian television has shown no new footage of Yeltsin for three weeks, a longer gap even than the 15 days between the heart surgery he underwent on November 5 and his first television appearance after the operation.
The press office said this morning that Yeltsin was working on papers but had no official meetings scheduled for Monday.
Doctors have said Yeltsin's latest health problems are not related to last November's operation. His heart problems kept him out of the Kremlin for most of the second half of last year.
